_comment: SxS Literature Review Quality — Run 1 of 2. paper_1 = paper-orc generated intro+RW; paper_2 = human-authored original intro+RW.
paper_1_analysis: Paper 1's Introduction proceeds in five paragraphs: (1) framing — what the LLM personality literature does and what silicon samples promise to do; (2) the prior measurement question and the standard human-subjects validation toolkit; (3) the empirical design of the audit with explicit data scale (375,700 API calls) and the directional-asymmetry finding (IPIP +0.29, SD3 -0.33); (4) the downstream cascade from item to model with three quantitative milestones (rho = -1.0, Tucker phi = 0.993, inter-model variance < 1%); (5) the persona stress test summarised as compliance without measurement validity. A 7-bullet contribution list closes the Introduction. The Related Work is organised into three structured subsections — LLM personality profiling and silicon samples; response styles, acquiescence, and social desirability; alignment, RLHF, and behavioural side effects — each closing with an explicit bridge-to-our-method synthesis sentence. Citation count is 57 unique works in Intro + RW (~110% of the assumed ACL/EMNLP baseline of ~52), including foundational anchors (Cronbach 1951; Couch & Keniston 1960; Crowne & Marlowe 1960; Kaiser 1958, 1960; Horn 1965; Tucker 1951; Meredith 1993; Vandenberg & Lance 2000) plus recent precedents (Suhr 2025; Pelet 2025; Han 2025; Sharma 2024; Acerbi 2024; Salecha 2024).
paper_2_analysis: Paper 2's Introduction proceeds in four paragraphs: (1) what the LLM personality literature does and the silicon-sample promise (5 citations); (2) the validity-check requirement (2 citations); (3) a list of six existing critiques as 'visible cracks' (Suhr, Tjuatja, Acerbi, Salecha, Pelet, Huang) with no synthesis; (4) the empirical design and the four-stage causal-chain summary in a single dense paragraph. The Related Work is organised into three subsections — Personality Measurement in LLMs; Response Style and Acquiescence Bias; Alignment Effects on LLM Behavior — each closing with an 'Our contribution' \paragraph that contrasts the present work with the cited literature. Citation count is 26 unique works in Intro + Related Work (~50% of the assumed ACL/EMNLP baseline), with the foundational psychometric methodological anchors (Kaiser, Horn, Tucker, Couch & Keniston, Crowne & Marlowe, Vandenberg & Lance, Meredith) absent from these sections. Cronbach 1951 and Lord & Novick 1968 are the only methodological foundations cited in the lit review.
comparison_justification: On Problem Framing and Motivation, both papers state the gap clearly; Paper 1's silicon-sample framing is more concrete about who inherits the measurement error. On Coverage of Prior Work, Paper 1 has more than twice the citations of Paper 2 (57 vs 26) and includes the foundational methodological anchors that Paper 2 omits. For a paper whose central thesis is that LLM-personality work has skipped the standard human-subjects validation toolkit, citing that toolkit explicitly is non-trivial — Paper 1 cites Cronbach 1951, Kaiser 1958/1960, Horn 1965, Tucker 1951, Meredith 1993, Vandenberg & Lance 2000, and Couch & Keniston 1960 in Related Work; Paper 2 omits all of these from Intro / Related Work. On Organization and Synthesis, both papers structure Related Work into three parallel subsections; Paper 1's overview → SOTA → limitation → bridge pattern provides slightly more explicit scaffolding than Paper 2's 'Our contribution' paragraph at the end of each subsection. On Positioning of the Contribution, Paper 1's 7-bullet itemised list at the end of the Introduction is sharper than Paper 2's prose-only contribution summary. On Writing Quality, both are clean; Paper 1 is slightly tighter, and Paper 2 has slightly more conversational subsection language ('The cracks are already visible. We do.'). The decisive criterion is Coverage of Prior Work: Paper 1's citation breadth, including foundational methodological anchors, is materially stronger.
